skill.name: trpc-scaffolder
skill.description: Scaffolds tRPC routers, procedure snippets, and Zod schemas for the DevPrep AI project structure.
skill.summary: Create consistent tRPC endpoint structures with Zod validation guidance and basic integration checks.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation syntax, relative imports, fixed project paths, or safe local validation commands. However, unescaped sed programs permit command execution, and unvalidated names permit path traversal. Public profile examples also omit authorization, and one error example exposes upstream details.

remediation.issue: Unescaped CLI values can inject sed commands.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers with a strict allowlist and replace dynamic sed programs with a template mechanism that treats values only as data.
Resolve each destination canonically, reject separators and dot segments, and verify that the result remains inside the intended output directory.

remediation.issue: Profile reads and updates use public procedures without ownership checks.
remediation.suggestion: Use protectedProcedure and compare the authenticated context identity with the requested user before reading or modifying profile data.

remediation.issue: An example exposes upstream API error messages to clients.
remediation.suggestion: Log detailed provider errors on the server and return a stable generic message with a non-sensitive correlation identifier.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated names permit path traversal
semantic_findings.description: Router and entity names are inserted into filesystem paths without validation. Crafted names can escape expected directories, create TypeScript files elsewhere, or probe existing files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The scripts preserve path separators from CLI arguments and concatenate the resulting values into paths. No allowlist, canonicalization, or containment check is present.

semantic_findings.title: Sed command injection in file generators
semantic_findings.description: Router and entity names are embedded directly into sed programs. Delimiters and newlines can inject sed commands, including GNU sed commands that execute a shell.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The replacement values are unescaped inside dynamically constructed sed expressions. A harmless local reproduction confirmed that an injected sed e command executes.

semantic_findings.title: Public profile procedures lack authorization
semantic_findings.description: The recommended router exposes profile reads and updates through publicProcedure using caller-supplied userId values. No session or ownership check prevents cross-user access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both procedures use publicProcedure and trust input.userId. The update path checks only record existence before modifying the selected profile.

semantic_findings.title: Upstream error details exposed to clients
semantic_findings.description: The error-handling example returns an upstream service error message through TRPCError. Provider details, request data, or operational information could reach clients.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly interpolates error.message into the client-facing TRPCError message. External API errors commonly include sensitive operational details.

content.value_statement: Manual tRPC setup creates repetitive router, schema, and registration work. This skill scaffolds consistent tRPC and Zod structures and checks basic project integration.
actual_capabilities: Creates router files from a TypeScript template.
Creates Zod schema files with inferred type placeholders.
Produces query or mutation procedure snippets for existing routers.
Checks router registration and schema type exports.
Provides examples for validation, errors, middleware, testing, pagination, and caching.
limitations: Scripts assume a DevPrep AI layout under frontend/src/lib/trpc.
Generated files require business logic, schema fields, and router registration.
Validation does not run TypeScript, tests, or security analysis.
Current scripts do not validate names before using them in paths and sed templates.

use_cases.title: Create a feature router
use_cases.description: Generate a router skeleton and registration guidance for a new application domain.

use_cases.title: Define endpoint contracts
use_cases.description: Create Zod input and output schema structures before implementing server behavior.

use_cases.title: Review tRPC consistency
use_cases.description: Check router registration, exported schema types, naming, authorization, and validation patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Zod schema for [entity] with these fields: [fields]. Export inferred input and output types.

prompt_templates.title: Add a procedure
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a [query or mutation] named [procedure] to [router]. Define its input, output, and required error cases.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a complete feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold [feature] with a router, Zod schemas, procedures, registration steps, and validation. Use protected procedures for sensitive operations.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing tRPC module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [module path] for schema coverage, authorization, error disclosure, registration, pagination, and tests. Propose focused corrections before editing.

output: A user router file with a typed procedure placeholder.

output_examples.input: Create schemas for a paginated question list.
output: Input schema guidance for limit and cursor values.
Output schema guidance for questions and the next cursor.

output_examples.output: A report of discovered routers, missing registration entries, schema files, and missing type exports.

best_practices: Replace every generated placeholder before using an endpoint.
Use protected procedures and ownership checks for sensitive data.
Run validation, TypeScript checks, and tests after scaffolding.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted or unvalidated names to the bundled scripts.
Do not expose account reads or mutations through public procedures.
Do not treat the validation script as a complete build or security check.

faq.question: Does this install tRPC or Zod?
faq.answer: No. The project must already include tRPC, Zod, and the expected directory structure.

faq.question: Does the router generator update _app.ts?
faq.answer: No. It creates the router file and prints manual registration steps.

faq.question: Does the procedure script edit an existing router?
faq.answer: No. It prints a procedure snippet for manual review and insertion.

faq.question: Can it generate protected procedures?
faq.answer: The templates use public procedures by default. Replace them and add authorization checks for sensitive operations.

faq.question: What does validation check?
faq.answer: It checks router files, registration patterns, schema files, and inferred type exports.

faq.question: Which names are safe for the scripts?
faq.answer: Until validation is added, use simple identifiers that start with a letter and contain only letters or numbers.
